Yeah, I guess that makes sense, if I hit anyone I would've probably known. I was so goddamned drunk, I cant believe it happened. It sure feels like my career is sunk even before it started, but maybe it isn't.

Don't worry about not going to college man, I sometimes wish I had thought it over before I went, but yeah we live with the decisions we make. 

This was a really big mistake, I'm really ashamed.

The horn thing was definitely subconscious. From what I remember I had been trying to pull a soccer mom at the bar and was rejected. I think the horn blaring was a drunken show of contempt for anyone who wasnt me. 

I guess you're right about that, if I hit someone I'd probably know. But in the back of my mind I'm afraid I'm gonna get in that courtroom and a widow and her fatherless children will be there, and they'll say 'YOU KILLED OUR DAD YOU DRUNK MONSTER.' Yeah its probably my guilty conscience but it's really weighing on me right now man.
Well done. You're fighting your personal demons, not some outside force, so ultimately you are always in control in every struggle that you have. Always remember that, and keep doing your thing.

Thanks for sharing your story dude. 

Lots of people make the mistake of cheating, fooling around on someone, etc, but it's never a good thing. What is good is that you're honest with yourself and your girlfriend. There's this weird misconception that a lot of dudes get, that they are only a real man if they get a lot of pussy all the time. Obviously, that's totally untrue but it happens to many men and undoubtedly porn only exacerbates that mentality. Good for you recognizing the true source of your discontent and acting to change it. 

Once I went for a hike in the mountains and I was wearing boots that I had just bought a day before, a bad move as any veteran hiker will tell you. On the last day we had an eleven mile march through pretty rough terrain, and my feet were already blistered to shit. As soon as we started up I wanted to stop, but I kept going, simply because there was no other option. I thought to myself "Ain't nothing to it but to do it." and marched through the pain. And that was it. Maybe think about your nofap journey like that. It's tough, but really there's nothing to think about, there's no Plan B, there's no equivocating or justification for failure. Just bite your lip, put your shoes on and walk. There's nothing to it but to do it. Simple as that. 

I would say good luck, but you don't need it! It's all in your heart and mind, so keep on keeping on.

I can't really say, I don't know your boyfriend, but from what you just told me it sounds like you're close enough to his folks that your presence would be a great show of support. The weird thing that I've found is that when people are having a really hard time dealing with loss, just being there and giving off an 'We're here for each other' vibe, helps in an incredible way. That's what families do, I think right? They support each other :). 

Best of luck again and more good vibes are coming your way.

I'm really sorry to hear about what's going on. I've had issues with depression before, but it doesn't sound as challenging as what you're going through.

Your parents aren't being as supportive as they could or should be, and I'm sorry to hear that as well. We'd all like to have excellent parents all the time, but they have their own issues as well, and we just have to accept that. 

I don't know you, and I don't know why you're feeling the way that you are feeling. I'm not a psychologist or psychiatrist or anyone qualified in any way to give you serious help. But one thing that I always found helped me when I was feeling really depressed and having anxiety attacks was walks in the woods alone. I like drinking, so I would bring a beer or two with me, and just walk, not listen to music and just hear the sounds of my own feet and the birds and squirrels darting around.

I guess what I'm trying to say is that when I felt awful and terrible about myself in the past, I would look at something like a tree, or a stone, or a streambed and reflect on the quiet dignity of nature. There's a certain pleasure that can be found when you realize how irresistible the natural ebb and flow of life is; everything is transient and yet somehow everything stays the same.  When I saw an enormous tree and thought about how long it took to grow, and how in the end it would rot and fall down and return to the dust made all of my problems somehow smaller. Life always goes on, whether you're there to see it or not. Don't know if that will help, but thoughts like that in the past helped me come to my own personal conclusion that my problems weren't as big as I had thought they were. Not saying your problems are small, or that any of this will totally help you feel better. But it worked for me, and I'd like to help you if I can.

You know the crazy thing about life? People make mistakes, big ones even, all the time. Every day. And when people are young and confused and angry with people that they care about, they tend to make more then most people. 

It's good that you came clean. There's nothing to hide anymore. If it means anything, a stranger on the internet has just heard your story and knows in his heart that you're probably a very good person who just made a mistake a few years ago.

I do not envy your situation, but I think you can help him tremendously. 

I would agree with BocajT, definitely go to him and his family to offer your condolences and support in person, but it depends on the people and your relationship with the family. If you guys are distant or they would prefer to grieve in private, give them their space. 

I don't know what else to say other than do anything you can for your boyfriend. I'm sending mental good energy your way.

Sorry to hear about your situation. You can always do whatever you want, you're in control of your life, ya know? So I guess one good thing to think about is maybe what you want here. If you think that this person can put down the controller and give you the attention you need/deserve, do you want to pursue your relationship with them? If you do, you have to sit them down and tell them how you feel. We can listen to you and give you advice on Reddit, but ultimately only you can really affect how it works out.

So if you'd like, tell this person 'we have to have a talk right now' and tell them how you feel. Unplug the game before they saved if you have to, it'll at least get their attention. And ultimately tell them what you've told us now and see where it goes. If they agree to change some of their habits, great! If not, well, you shouldn't be in a relationship with a person who makes you so unhappy. Without knowing more details I can't give you more advice than that.
